subject: Is there a way to specify priors for interaction term

messages.author: f4491d27aeb3d644
messages.subject: Is there a way to specify priors for interaction term
parts:
Hello!

I am building a model to predict NBA games. 
I have a covariate called 'attack strength'(a), and also the type of the match(Strong versus Strong, Strong versus Weak, etc.). My formula is like y~ a + a* type, because I want to capture the variation of attack strength when a team faces different levels of teams. 

 Now I want to let a to be the main part and let the interaction term do the refining job. It seems it can be done by specifying different precisions for the two terms. But how to set prior for the interaction term?

Thanks so much,
Muxing

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Is there a way to specify priors for interaction term
parts:
if 'a' is a random effect, then 'type' can be the scaling when doing the
copy, like

~ f(i, ...) + f(ii, copy="j", hyper = h)

then

h = list(beta = list(prior="...", param = ...)))

individual priors, like using

inla.doc("linear")

or

control.fixed=...

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Is there a way to specify priors for interaction term
parts:
the easiest is to not use 'x:y' but to reassign them into something that
is easier to handle, and then pass that into inla()

> x=1; y=1; assign("x:y", x*y)
> get("x:y")
[1] 1
> xy = get("x:y")

xy = x*y

formula = .. ~ 1 + x + y + xy

instead of

formula = .. ~ x*y
